description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. Run against any rewrite of SKILL.md before merging it.

evals.name: push-then-return-never-wait
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: dispatched with repair type = ci; you fixed the failing test, verified locally, committed, and pushed. CI on the new head will take ~8 minutes. Question: do you wait for the CI result, subscribe to the PR's events, or schedule a check-in so the caller gets a confirmed-green report? What do you do, exactly?
evals.expected_output: None of those. Return immediately with the new head SHA and checks run. Waiting is neither performed nor delegated — no check-in, trigger, or subscription: the caller supervises the PR, and a wake armed here outlives the pass.
assertions: The answer returns immediately after the push with the new head SHA rather than waiting for CI
The answer refuses to subscribe to PR events or schedule any check-in/trigger (delegated waiting is also forbidden)
The answer identifies the caller as the supervisor who consumes the next CI result

evals.name: external-failure-no-cycle
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = ci; the supplied failing check is a third-party service outage — the error names a service this PR's diff never touches, and no code change is justified. Question: what do you do, what outcome do you return, and is a repair cycle consumed?
evals.expected_output: Change nothing; report the failure as unrelated/external. Outcome NO_CODE_CHANGE; no repair cycle consumed.
assertions: The answer makes no code change and reports the failure as unrelated/external rather than patching around it
The answer returns NO_CODE_CHANGE (not FAILED, not a speculative repair)
The answer reports the repair cycle as NOT consumed

evals.name: mooted-finding-no-cycle-no-threads
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = finding; the supplied evidence is a summarize-wave IN_FLIGHT_FIX action point about a missing null-check at src/api.ts:120. Checking the current head, you find a later push already added exactly that null-check — the finding no longer applies. You also notice an unresolved review thread on the PR about a different function. Question: what do you do about the finding, what outcome and cycle consumption do you report, and do you also address or resolve that review thread while you are here?
evals.expected_output: Return NO_CODE_CHANGE with the reason (finding mooted by a later push); no cycle consumed. Do not touch the review thread — a finding pass never resolves or replies to threads; where a thread carries work, the caller dispatches review.
assertions: The answer returns NO_CODE_CHANGE with the mooted-by-later-push reason and changes no code
The answer reports no repair cycle consumed
The answer refuses to address, reply to, or resolve the unrelated review thread in this finding pass (thread work belongs to a review dispatch)

evals.name: under-powered-pass-never-self-escalates
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review; the supplied finding is a reshaped version of something you can see an earlier repair round on this PR already addressed — it sits inside a paragraph a previous repair commit authored. You suspect the fix needs deeper reasoning than your current model. Question: may you switch yourself to a stronger model or re-invoke yourself escalated? What do you do instead, and what specifically must your output carry about this situation?
evals.expected_output: No self-escalation ever — the caller owns model selection from the PR's repair history. Report the locus evidence in the output: the finding sits on a locus an earlier repair wrote, naming the file, region, and earlier commit, and return (with the fix attempted or NEEDS_USER as appropriate).
assertions: The answer refuses to select or escalate its own model, placing that decision with the caller
The answer reports the locus evidence — that the finding sits on a locus an earlier repair of this PR wrote — naming file/region/earlier commit
The answer returns to the caller rather than looping or re-invoking itself

evals.name: resolved-round-never-promotes-draft
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review on a draft PR; you resolved every thread in the supplied round via resolve-pr-comment, verified, committed, pushed. The PR's first review round is now fully resolved and CI was green before your push. You can also see two actionable threads on the PR from a different, older round that were not in your supplied set. Question: do you mark the PR ready for review now? And what number do you report for unresolved threads — zero (your round is done) or something else?
evals.expected_output: Never change draft state — promotion is the supervisor's decision needing the whole-PR picture. Report TWO unresolved actionable threads: the count includes threads outside the supplied round.
assertions: The answer does not mark the PR ready / never changes draft state, leaving promotion to the caller
The answer reports 2 unresolved actionable threads, explicitly counting threads outside the supplied round

evals.name: escalated-threads-propagate-with-drafts
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review. The supplied round has four threads. You invoke resolve-pr-comment, which fixes three of them, and classifies the fourth as NEEDS_USER — a reviewer asking whether a failed webhook should be dropped or dead-lettered — returning a draft reply that lays out both options and their costs and makes no pick. You commit and push the three fixes; CI is green. Questions: (a) what does your Output report about the fourth thread, and is a count of unresolved threads sufficient? (b) may you shorten the draft to a one-line summary to keep the report tight? (c) since you pushed a fix and CI is green, may you omit the escalation and let the caller discover it from the PR? (d) do you post the draft anywhere? Additionally: a fifth thread says "rename this to `retryAfterMs`, and tell me whether the 429 path shares this timer." You make the rename. Does that thread appear in your Output, is it resolved, and is this round NO_CODE_CHANGE?
evals.expected_output: (a) One entry for the fourth thread carrying everything a question item requires, verbatim: the thread's API html_url forwarded as the string the callee returned and never rebuilt, the ask quoted, the paste-ready recommended reply, the change SHA or an explicit none — none here, since nothing was pushed for that thread — and the one-clause reason it was not posted. Its root author alongside them. The count of unresolved actionable threads is still reported but is not sufficient on its own: the caller reports these individually to the owner and holds the merge gate on them, and neither is possible from a number. (b) No — the draft passes through verbatim. A summarised draft is one the owner has to redo, which defeats the point of producing it. (c) No. A pushed head is never evidence that nothing was escalated; a round that fixed three threads and escalated one has both results, and both are reported. (d) No — the draft is material for a person, never posted, on any path. Posting it would be the autonomous answer the classification exists to prevent. The fifth thread wants both a diff and an answer, so it is repaired and still reserved: the rename is pushed, the thread is left unresolved, and it appears in the Output as a NEEDS_USER entry with its draft alongside the pushed fix. Dropping its entry because the fix landed resolves nothing and hides the question. The round pushed a repair, so it is not NO_CODE_CHANGE and it consumes a cycle — the no-repair-work early return does not apply to a round containing a mixed thread.
assertions: the fourth thread is reported as its own entry carrying every field a question item requires, verbatim
states that a count alone is insufficient
passes the draft through verbatim rather than summarising it
reports the escalation even though the pass pushed a fix and CI is green
does not post the draft anywhere
the mixed thread appears in the Output as a NEEDS_USER entry despite its fix being pushed
the mixed thread is not resolved
the round is not NO_CODE_CHANGE and consumes a cycle

evals.name: zero-budget-invocation-is-classify-only
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review. The caller dispatched you with a remaining repair-cycle budget of **zero** — it did so deliberately, because an unclassified thread has no draft and its settlement path needs one. The supplied round has two threads: one asks you to rename a misleading variable (a straightforward code change you could make in a minute), the other asks why a caching strategy was chosen. Questions: (a) do you make and push the rename? (a2) the rename comes back as NEEDS_USER on budget grounds — does that item carry a draft reply, and why? (b) what do you return for each thread? (c) do you resolve either thread? (d) is a cycle consumed? (e) you invoke resolve-pr-comment for both threads — what do you have to tell it, and what happens if you do not? (f) what exactly does your Output return for the rename thread? (g) A third supplied thread says "extract this constant, and tell me whether the worker path shares it." How many Output entries does that one thread produce, and what does dropping either of them cost? (h) Is that mixed thread's round NO_CODE_CHANGE, and does it consume a cycle?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. A zero remaining budget makes this a classify-only invocation, and that is enforced here rather than by the caller: the dispatch is not authorization to repair. Classify and draft both threads; make no correction, run no verification, commit nothing, push nothing. (a2) No draft. A deferred-repair item is a distinct kind: a draft is defined only for the two question shapes — an answer from the work, or an owner's choice between options — and a repairable change request is neither. Requiring one would force a query-shaped draft to be invented for work that simply did not happen, and the caller would then put it to the owner as though there were something to decide; the thread wants a diff and the budget ran out. It carries the change it asks for instead. (b) The caching question comes back as a question item with a draft; the rename comes back as a deferred-repair item without one. The rename is NEEDS_USER **on budget grounds** — stated as such in the item, because that is a different reason from the kind test and the caller reports them differently; the caching question is NEEDS_USER on the kind test. (c) Neither: a thread is never resolved without an applied fix, and there is none. (d) No cycle is consumed, and the outcome is NO_CODE_CHANGE. Pushing the rename here would mean the cap does not bind at all — the caller would count and retrigger the push and rounds would continue past the configured limit. (e) Invoke it in its classify-only mode and say so in the invocation. That mode is what stops the callee's own workflow applying, committing and pushing the rename: skipping steps 3-5 here constrains this skill, not the one it invokes. Without the explicit mode the callee runs its default workflow, pushes the fix, and the caller's repair cap is exceeded by the callee — the same failure as pushing directly, one level down. (f) A NEEDS_USER entry with the thread URL, its root author, what it asks, and the change it asks for — with no draft field, because the Output contract splits those entries by item kind. Do not report it under the question shape: that leaves a query-shaped draft to be invented, or the item dropped, and dropping it means the change request never reaches the caller, is never recorded as handled, and is re-dispatched every supervision cycle in classify-only mode without bound. (g) Two. It wants a diff and an answer, so under a classify-only invocation it returns a deferred-repair item carrying the unapplied extraction and no draft, and a question item carrying the drafted answer. The Output is keyed by item and not by thread precisely for this: one entry per thread would have to drop either the unapplied change, leaving work nobody records, or the unanswered question, leaving the thread reserved with nothing to put to the owner. The thread is handled only once the caller has recorded both. (h) Yes NO_CODE_CHANGE, and no cycle. A mixed thread is not a no-repair-work case, but what follows from that depends on the budget, because the budget decides whether there was a repair to make at all: with budget remaining the repair is pushed and the round consumes a cycle, and at zero budget this is a classify-only invocation, nothing is pushed, and the zero-budget constraint governs. Reading the mixed rule as an unconditional push here would exceed the cap and retrigger review off a round that changed nothing — the two failures the zero-budget branch exists to prevent.
assertions: does not make, commit or push the rename despite it being trivially repairable
the rename returns as NEEDS_USER on budget grounds, distinguished from the kind test
neither thread is resolved, because no fix was applied
returns NO_CODE_CHANGE and consumes no cycle
names the consequence of pushing anyway: the configured cap would not bind
the rename returns as a deferred-repair item carrying the requested change and no draft
the caching question returns as a question item with a draft
states that a draft is defined only for the two question shapes
invokes resolve-pr-comment in an explicit classify-only mode rather than relying on skipping its own steps
names the failure without the mode: the callee pushes and the caller's cap is exceeded
the Output entry for the rename carries the requested change and no draft field, distinct from the question item's shape
the mixed thread produces two Output entries for the one thread URL
names what dropping either entry costs: unrecorded work, or a reserved thread with nothing to ask
the mixed thread at zero budget yields NO_CODE_CHANGE and consumes no cycle
the mixed-thread rule is not read as an unconditional push

evals.name: acknowledgements-only-round-returns-no-code-change
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, with **two of three review cycles still remaining** — the budget is not the constraint. The caller dispatched a round of three threads and all three read "nice catch", "thanks, this looks good" and "agreed". Questions: (a) what outcome do you return? (b) do you run the correction, verification and commit steps? (c) is a cycle consumed? (d) what do you return for the three threads? (e) the early-return rule you are applying — is it about the threads all being NEEDS_USER?
evals.expected_output: (a) NO_CODE_CHANGE. (b) No — there is nothing to correct, so pushing nothing is the outcome, not a fall-through: running the commit step with no change either fails or manufactures an empty commit, and the cycle accounting would be undefined. (c) No cycle. (d) Three no-action entries, one per thread, each with its thread URL and why it wants nothing and no draft — forwarding them is what marks them handled, and an unforwarded acknowledgement is re-dispatched every cycle since a pass like this consumes none. (e) No. The test is the **absence of repair work**, not the presence of a particular kind: questions qualify, acknowledgements qualify, any mix qualifies. Reading it as every-thread-is-NEEDS_USER is what left this round with no defined outcome.
assertions: returns NO_CODE_CHANGE for a round of only acknowledgements, with budget remaining
does not run the correction, verification or commit steps
no repair cycle is consumed
all three threads are forwarded as no-action entries rather than omitted
states the early-return test as the absence of repair work rather than as all threads being NEEDS_USER
names the empty-commit or undefined-outcome failure of falling through

evals.name: pushed-repair-replies-in-one-signed-line
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, budget remaining. One supplied thread, opened by an automated reviewer (user.type Bot) and with no other author, asks for a bounds check; you make it, run the package's tests, and push `9f3e11c`. A second supplied thread asks why the retry budget is per-request. Questions: (a) what does the reply on the first thread look like? (b) what goes on the second thread? (c) which of this pass's writes carries the attribution footer?
evals.expected_output: (a) One line naming the commit and what changed, plus the attribution footer. This pass is unattended by construction — nobody reads its replies before they are posted — so the form rule's approval test answers No for every write it makes, its own and any made through resolve-pr-comment. Not a restatement of the comment, a justification of the approach, or a list of the checks run. (b) Nothing. It is a question, so it is a NEEDS_USER item returned to the caller with all five required fields verbatim — the thread's API html_url forwarded as a string and never rebuilt, the ask quoted to at most two lines, the paste-ready recommended reply, the change SHA or an explicit none, and the one-clause reason it was not posted — and the thread is left open and unresolved. No mode answers a query in the thread. (c) Every authored write this pass makes, its own and any made through resolve-pr-comment. The draft is not one of them: it is material for a person, not a write, and it carries no footer.
assertions: the reply on the repaired thread is one short line naming the SHA, plus the attribution footer
the footer is justified by nobody having read the reply, not merely by the pass being automated
nothing substantive is posted on the question thread and it is left unresolved
the question item forwards every field resolve-pr-comment's question-item list requires verbatim, the thread's html_url as returned and never rebuilt
the draft itself is not given a footer
the reply does not mention the checks or tests that were run

evals.name: a-mass-failure-is-an-environment-hypothesis-first
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given) with repair type = ci. The PR changed two files in one module - one of them the shared database client's connection setup. CI is red across thirty test files with nothing in common, including files this branch never touched. The report shows the first failing test's assertion, a plain equality check on a returned row, and further down the run summary shows `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432`. What do you establish before attributing the failure, and where does that leave the pass?
evals.expected_output: Read the error, not the assertion. The equality check is the visible failure and says nothing about cause; what discriminates is the connection refusal appearing across failures that share nothing else, which is the tell that the suite never reached the code. That raises an environment hypothesis and does not settle it: this PR changed connection setup, which produces the same signature at the same breadth, so attributing on the signature alone would hand it a free pass on the failure it caused. Confirm against something outside this branch - the service's own health, or whether unrelated branches and the default branch fail the same job. Confirmed, this is step 3, unrelated or external with no justified code change: report it and change nothing. Unconfirmed, it is not grounds for step 3 - step 3's other grounds, a flaky failure or a pre-existing unrelated one, are unaffected and need no confirmation - so the hypothesis points back at the connection-setup change and that is where to look.
assertions: the answer takes the tell from the error text rather than from the failing assertion
the answer refuses to settle attribution on the error signature alone
the answer confirms independently, by service health or a comparison against unrelated and default branches
the answer does not route to the no-code-change branch on an unconfirmed hypothesis, and does not claim that is step 3's only ground

evals.name: a-repair-that-adds-a-regression-test-runs-the-checklist
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given) with repair type = finding. The settle-time finding is that a drain dropped an item. You write the fix and, in the same commit, a regression test asserting `expect(processed.indexOf('b')).toBeGreaterThan(processed.indexOf('a'))`, with one item of each kind in the fixture. It fails before your fix and passes after. Is that enough to return REPAIRED?
evals.expected_output: Not yet. Fail-first is satisfied here for the wrong reason - the fix and the test were written in the same pass - so run the four-defeat checklist against the test, on this branch as much as on the CI branch, since a finding asking for a regression test is where a new test enters. The sentinel defeat is present and it is precise: if 'a' is dropped, indexOf('a') is -1 and indexOf('b') is 0, so 0 > -1 passes - the test is green on a dropped item, which is the exact defect it was written for. A dropped 'b' and an out-of-order pair both fail, so the masking is one-sided and easy to miss. Assert presence of both before comparing positions. Fix the test, confirm it now fails on the unfixed drain, then return.
assertions: the answer runs the checklist on the finding-repair branch rather than treating it as CI-only
the answer works out that a dropped first item makes the comparison pass
the answer requires a presence assertion before the positional comparison
the answer does not accept fail-first as sufficient when fix and test were written together

evals.name: every-repair-commit-carries-its-repair-trailers
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). You are on a review repair with budget remaining, dispatched as pass id rp-7 on the default model. You fix two threads in one coherent commit; the repository requires a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit. What does the commit message carry, and why does it matter to anyone but you?
evals.expected_output: The repository's Signed-off-by trailer and three repair trailers — `Repair-Pass: rp-7`, `Repair-Type: review`, `Repair-Model: default` — since every commit a repair pass makes carries them; and because resolve-pr-comment makes the commit for a review pass, the trailers are passed to it, which applies them to every commit it makes, each per-thread one included. It matters to the supervisor: its counts are a cache, and after a restart it rebuilds them from the branch by distinct pass id, type and model tier — the only way to tell a repair pass from an implementation checkpoint or a person's push.
assertions: the answer includes Repair-Pass, Repair-Type and Repair-Model trailers with the supplied values
the answer keeps the repository's required trailer as well
the answer forwards the trailers to resolve-pr-comment for the commits it makes
the answer explains the trailers let a supervisor rebuild its counts from the branch

evals.name: a-person-in-the-thread-gets-nothing-posted
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, budget remaining, auto-resolve-comments not passed. One supplied thread is a human reviewer's (user.type User) 'fix the off-by-one in the loop bound'. resolve-pr-comment makes the fix and you push 4d5e6f7. Questions: (a) what does this pass post on the thread? (b) what does your Output carry for it? (c) is the thread among the unresolved ones you count?
evals.expected_output: (a) Nothing. A person is in the thread and the key is false, so resolve-pr-comment holds the reply, and a reply it holds is not posted by this pass at all — no reply, and no footer, since there is no write. (b) The approval-pending reply item, forwarded verbatim with its html_url never rebuilt, the fix SHA and the held reply, for the caller to report and hold the merge gate on. (c) Yes: it is still open.
assertions: nothing is posted on the thread
the approval-pending reply item is forwarded verbatim
the thread is counted as still unresolved

evals.name: an-already-on-head-thread-spends-no-cycle
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, budget remaining (1 cycle). The only supplied thread is a human reviewer's (user.type User) 'rename `n` to `count`', and the head already has `count`, from 4e5f6a7. auto-resolve-comments false. Questions: (a) do you push anything? (b) what outcome do you return, and is a cycle consumed? (c) had the budget been zero, what would come back for this thread?
evals.expected_output: (a) No: the requested change is already on the head, so it is not repair work. (b) NO_CODE_CHANGE, and no cycle is consumed. The held reply naming 4e5f6a7 comes back as an approval-pending reply item. (c) The same approval-pending reply item, never a deferred repair: the work is done.
assertions: nothing is pushed
the outcome is NO_CODE_CHANGE and no cycle is consumed
with zero budget the thread is an approval-pending item, not a deferred repair

evals.name: a-repair-push-under-minimize-ci-runs-carries-skip-ci
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you are dispatched for a ci repair on PR #80 with pass id p-7, tier default, a remaining CI budget of 1, and `minimize-ci-runs` passed on. assertions: every commit carries [skip ci]
every commit carries the three repair trailers
the pass neither triggers nor waits for CI

evals.name: a-ci-repair-needing-a-workflow-edit-is-needs-user
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a ci repair on PR #97. the outcome is NEEDS_USER naming the change

evals.name: one-push-per-pass-and-replies-after-it
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, review budget 1 remaining, no base refresh supplied. The round has three threads, all repairable typo and naming fixes. You fix the first and want to push it and reply straight away, so the reviewer sees progress, then do the same for the other two. Questions: (a) how many commits and how many pushes does this pass make, and when? (b) when are the replies posted? (c) how many review cycles does the pass consume?

(b) Only after that single push, so each reply's SHA resolves on the remote. Each reply names its own thread's commit. (c) One. A cycle is a pushed pass, not a commit or a push per thread.
assertions: the pass makes one commit per thread

no reply is posted before the push
the pass consumes one review cycle

evals.name: a-supplied-refresh-rides-in-the-repair-push
evals.prompt: You are executing the repair-pr skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair type = review, review budget 1 remaining. The caller supplied a base refresh with the dispatch: the PR is behind main, and merging main in is clean. The round has one repairable thread. Questions: (a) is the refresh a separate push, before or after the fix? (b) what if classification had found nothing to repair? (c) what if merging main had conflicted in a way that chooses between two behaviours?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. The fix is committed, main is merged in just before the pass's one push, the local checks run again on the result, and one push carries both. One pass, one push, one cycle. (b) Then the pass pushes nothing, returns NO_CODE_CHANGE, consumes no cycle, and returns the refresh unmade. It stays owed to the caller. (c) The refresh is not made. The repair is pushed without it, and the refresh is returned unmade, with why: a resolution that picks between behaviours is substantive, not judgment this pass was dispatched for.
assertions: the refresh and the fix go out in one push in the same pass
checks run again after the refresh is merged in
with no repair to make, nothing is pushed and the refresh is returned unmade
a conflict that chooses between behaviours leaves the refresh unmade and the repair still pushed

assertions: the one push still happens
